holidays.name: Monkey Day
holidays.description: A gleefully silly day for celebrating all things simian. People dress up in monkey costumes, throw themed parties, make art and swap banana-based snacks. Primates of every kind are welcome, including apes, lemurs and your cousin who climbs everything.
holidays.origin: Monkey Day began in 2000, when art students Casey Sorrow and Eric Millikin at Michigan State University scribbled it onto a calendar. It spread through webcomics and the internet, and it is now observed around the world.
holidays.funFact: What began as a doodle on a campus calendar grew into a global event with parties, art shows and charity drives for primate conservation.

holidays.name: National Bouillabaisse Day
holidays.description: A day to dive into the saffron-scented fish stew of the French Mediterranean. A proper bouillabaisse simmers several kinds of fish with tomato, fennel, garlic and orange peel. It is often served with crusty bread and a garlicky rouille.
holidays.origin: Bouillabaisse comes from the port city of Marseille, where fishermen cooked the bony rockfish they couldn't sell at market. The dish grew from a humble seaside meal into a celebrated classic. The day itself is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin.
holidays.funFact: Marseille restaurants signed a 'Bouillabaisse Charter' in 1980 that spells out which fish belong in an authentic pot.

holidays.name: Roast Chestnuts Day
holidays.description: A cozy celebration of warm, smoky, sweet chestnuts roasted over an open fire or in the oven. It is the perfect excuse to score the shells, burn your fingertips a little, and enjoy a snack that tastes like winter.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin, but it fits neatly into the holiday season. Roasting chestnuts is an old winter tradition across Europe, Asia and North America, and the snack is sold by street vendors in many cities.
holidays.funFact: Chestnuts must be scored before roasting, because the steam inside can make unscored nuts burst with a pop.
